key_insight: Reinforcement learning guides adaptive grid refinement for the Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equation, concentrating nodes where discretization error is large to support accurate optimal feedback control.
engineering_relevance: Adaptive node placement could reduce computational demands for feedback-control design compared with fixed grids while better resolving difficult regions of state space.
method: Solve the HJB PDE to obtain optimal feedback control.
Use an RL-based strategy to dynamically refine the computational grid.
Target fewer total nodes with higher density in high-error regions.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes the approach and its intended benefits but reports no benchmarks, numerical accuracy gains, or node-count reductions.
watch_item: Scalability and net computational savings remain unestablished, especially when accounting for RL overhead in high-dimensional state spaces.
paper_title: Adaptive Grid Refinement for Optimal Feedback Control
